transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Yeah, well, I guess I decided to come in because things have just been a little... off lately. I supervise a construction crew—mostly residential builds right now—and honestly, the delays lately are just a nightmare. We had this massive hold-up on drywall last week, and I spent practically half my day just arguing with the supplier on the phone. And then on top of that, I have to go to these neighborhood zoning meetings that just drag on forever. Like on Tuesday, this woman, Mrs. Higgins, complained for forty-five minutes about the noise from the excavators. It’s a construction site, you know? What does she expect? 

Anyway, sorry, um... what made me actually make the appointment is that after those really long days on site, or after one of those awful neighborhood meetings, I’ll come home and just... I end up eating way more than I ever meant to. I'll just stand in the kitchen and go through whatever’s there. Leftover takeout, bowls of cereal, bags of chips... I just keep going until I’m so uncomfortably full that I feel sick. It's just getting frustrating.
Do you usually feel stressed, anxious, or upset right before you start eating excessively?

I mean, I'm not really sure. I haven't really stopped to notice if I'm feeling a specific way right in that exact moment before it happens. I guess I'm just always kind of stressed? 

Like, take my foreman, Dave. He’s been doing this for fifteen years, and yesterday he completely messed up the framing on a load-bearing wall. I had to stand there in the mud—because of course it was pouring rain—explaining the blueprints to him like he was a first-year apprentice. And the whole time, the client is texting me non-stop. I swear, people watch one season of some home renovation show and suddenly they think they know more than the general contractor. They want custom arches but don't want to pay for the structural engineer to approve it. It’s wild. I actually had to turn my phone on silent yesterday just to hear myself think over the generators. 

But, um... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, if I'm upset right before I eat. Yeah, I don't know, I just haven't really tracked my mood like that. It's hard to say.
Do you think eating helps you feel better after a long or stressful day?

I don't know if it makes me feel better, exactly. Maybe? Honestly, I don't really think about it like that, I just do it. It's kind of like... well, it's like when you're trying to fix a bad pour on a foundation, right? You just keep adding cement trying to level it out, but you're not really fixing the underlying issue, you're just making a bigger mess. 

Speaking of messes, you wouldn't believe the site I was at this morning. The plumbers came in to do the rough-in for the master bath, and they completely ignored the updated schematics I sent them on Monday. I mean, I emailed them, I texted the lead guy, I even printed out a physical copy and taped it to the framing. And what do they do? They run the pipes right through where the custom vanity is supposed to go. Now I have to get them back out here, which is going to push the drywall guys back, and the client is already breathing down my neck about the timeline because they want to host some big Thanksgiving dinner in a house that currently doesn't even have walls. I just... I don't understand how people can be so bad at their jobs. 

But yeah, I don't really know if eating makes me feel better. I haven't really thought about it.
Do you usually feel guilty after eating so much?

I mean, I don't really know if guilt is the right word. I guess I haven't really analyzed how I feel afterward, you know? I just feel... full. Uncomfortably full. 

But honestly, the thing that makes me feel guilty is when I have to tell a client that their move-in date is delayed again. Like, I have this one couple right now, they're expecting a baby in two months, and they are so stressed about getting into the new house. And I had to sit them down yesterday and explain that the custom windows they ordered—the ones they absolutely *had* to have—are stuck on a cargo ship somewhere in the Pacific. I felt terrible, but what am I supposed to do? I can't build the windows myself. And then the husband started asking if we could just board up the openings temporarily so they could move in. I had to explain to a grown man why we can't just slap some plywood over a giant hole in the wall and call it a day, especially with a newborn. It's like people lose all common sense when they're building a house. 

So yeah, dealing with that kind of stuff makes me feel guilty, I guess. But with the food? I don't know, I just haven't really thought about it.
Do you feel like you can stop eating once you've started, or does it feel like you can't control how much you're eating?

I mean, yeah, I guess that's the thing. Once I start on those evenings, it feels like I'm completely on autopilot. Like, I'm literally standing there telling myself to stop because I have an early crew start the next day, but I'm still going back to the kitchen for more. It's like I can't hit the brakes. 

Which is ironic, because I spend my entire day telling people to hit the brakes. Like this morning, I had a guy on the excavator who decided he didn't need to wait for the utility locate flags to be marked before he started trenching for the new sewer line. I saw him from across the lot and had to literally sprint through the mud waving my arms like a maniac to get him to stop. I mean, do you know what happens if you hit a main gas line? Best case scenario, the whole neighborhood gets evacuated and we're fined thousands of dollars. Worst case, well, we're all blown to pieces. And he just looked at me from the cab like I was overreacting! I swear, the safety protocols on these sites are treated like suggestions half the time. If I wasn't there constantly breathing down their necks, they'd probably try to wire the electrical panels while standing in a puddle. 

But yeah, with the food... it's like I'm the guy in the excavator, you know? I know I should stop, I'm telling myself to stop, but I just keep digging anyway.
Do you feel like you have a choice about whether or not to eat when you start eating on those evenings?

I guess... no, I don't really feel like I have a choice. It's exactly like I said, I'm just on autopilot. I'll be standing right there in the kitchen, physically telling myself, "You need to stop, you have to be on site at 5:30 AM to meet the concrete trucks," but my hands are just grabbing more stuff out of the pantry anyway. 

Speaking of concrete trucks, you wouldn't believe the nightmare I had with the dispatcher yesterday. I ordered three trucks for a foundation pour, right? Specifically requested a 4000 PSI mix with a retarder because it was supposed to be 90 degrees out. Well, the first truck shows up an hour late, which means the crew is just standing around on the clock doing nothing. And then, when the driver finally hands me the ticket, I see they sent a standard 3000 PSI mix. No retarder. I had to reject the load right there on the spot. The driver was furious, the dispatcher was yelling at me on the phone, but what am I supposed to do? If I pour that mix in that heat, it's going to flash set before we can even get it screeded, and then I've got a ruined foundation that I have to pay to jackhammer out. It's like nobody pays attention to the details anymore. You have to double-check every single thing or people will just screw it up and expect you to deal with the fallout. 

But yeah, with the eating... it just doesn't feel like a choice. I'm telling myself to stop, but I just keep going back for more.
Do you think the eating happens more often on days when you've had particularly stressful events at work?

I mean, maybe? I haven't really tracked it like that. I guess I'm always stressed at work, so it's hard to tell if it's worse on certain days. 

Like, take yesterday for example. I had to deal with the electrical inspector. This guy, I swear he wakes up every morning and decides how he's going to make my life miserable. We had a rough-in inspection for a custom build, and he failed us because one of the outlet boxes in the kitchen island was a quarter of an inch too low according to some obscure local code amendment that they just passed last month. A quarter of an inch! I had the electrician right there, and he was ready to just rip the whole thing out and start over, he was so mad. I had to spend forty-five minutes calming him down and then another hour negotiating with the inspector to let us just adjust the bracket instead of rewiring the whole circuit. It's exhausting. You spend half your day just managing adult toddlers who throw tantrums when things don't go exactly their way. 

But as for the food... I don't know if the stressful days make it happen more. It just kind of happens when it happens, I guess. I haven't really noticed a pattern.
Do you think the eating happens as a way to deal with the stress you experience at work?

I don't really know if it's about the stress. I mean, I guess it could be? But like I said, I'm pretty much always stressed, so it's not like I can point to a bad day and say, "Oh, that's why I ate." It just feels like it's something I do. 

Honestly, if I wanted to eat every time I was stressed, I'd never stop eating. Like, this morning, the framing crew showed up short two guys. Apparently, one of them threw his back out over the weekend, and the other one just didn't bother to call in. So suddenly I'm looking at a schedule that's already tight, and I've got half a crew trying to lift these massive LVL beams into place for the second-floor joists. I actually had to jump in and help them muscle one of those things up the ladders because we didn't have the crane scheduled until tomorrow. My shoulders are still killing me. And then, right in the middle of all that, the homeowner decides to drop by unannounced for a "quick walkthrough." She's walking around in open-toed sandals, pointing at the framing and asking if we can just move a load-bearing wall two feet to the left so her kitchen island will have better flow. I had to smile and nod and explain that no, we can't just move a structural wall without getting an engineer to redraw the plans and pulling new permits, which would delay the project by at least three weeks. She looked at me like I was just being difficult on purpose. 

So yeah, the stress is just... it's always there. I don't know if the eating is really about that or not. It's just something that happens.
Do you think eating helps you cope with the stress you experience at work?

I don't really know if it helps. I mean, maybe in the exact second I'm doing it? But usually, I just feel terrible afterward, so it's not a very good coping mechanism if it is one. 

Coping is just... I don't know. You should see how some of my crew copes with stress. Like my lead drywaller, Terry. He copes by taking these ridiculous smoke breaks every forty-five minutes. I caught him yesterday out by his truck when he was supposed to be mudding the master bath, just chain-smoking and screaming on the phone to his ex-wife about child support. And I'm just standing there in the doorway, waiting for him to wrap it up so we can actually stay on schedule for the painters who are coming Thursday. 

Which, by the way, the painters are a whole other headache. They always demand that the HVAC is running so the paint cures faster, but the HVAC guys haven't even installed the registers yet because the supplier sent the wrong finish. We specifically ordered brushed nickel, and they sent three boxes of oil-rubbed bronze. Who even uses oil-rubbed bronze anymore? It looks like it belongs in some 2005 McMansion. I literally had to load up forty heavy metal registers into the back of my truck and drive them back to the supply house myself, which killed two whole hours of my afternoon. 

So... yeah, I'm not really sure. I guess I haven't really thought about whether the eating actually helps with any of that. It's just kind of a blur.
Do you usually eat like this immediately after a stressful event at work?

I don't think it's like an immediate reaction, no. It's not like I get off a bad phone call and instantly go eat. It's more just... later, maybe? I don't really track the timing. 

Speaking of timing, though, you wouldn't believe the scheduling nightmare I'm dealing with for the concrete pour on this new foundation. We were supposed to pour on Tuesday, right? But the meteorologist decides to predict a ninety percent chance of thunderstorms, so I have to call the concrete plant and push it to Thursday. Well, Thursday comes, and the weather is beautiful, not a cloud in the sky—but the pump truck breaks down on the highway. Just completely blows a transmission or something. So the concrete is sitting in the mixer trucks, getting hot, and the drivers are getting antsy because if that stuff sets up in the drum, they have to literally jackhammer it out. I spent three hours frantically calling every other pump company in a fifty-mile radius, begging someone to send a truck out. I finally found a guy, but he charged me double the standard rate just because he knew I was desperate. And then the homeowner was upset because the noise was bothering their neighbor's dog. A dog! We're pouring a foundation, of course it's loud. 

So yeah, I don't really know if the eating happens right after something stressful. I just haven't noticed if there's a connection like that.
Do you typically eat this way on days when nothing particularly stressful has happened at work?

I mean, I don't really know. Honestly, it's hard to even remember a day when nothing stressful happens. I guess maybe? But I couldn't tell you for sure. 

Like, even on days that are supposed to be "easy," something always comes up. Take last Friday. We were just doing final punch-list items on a remodel. It was supposed to be a half-day. But then the cabinet guy shows up to install the custom range hood, and he realizes he measured wrong. The whole thing was an inch and a half too wide to fit between the upper cabinets. And these are custom, inset shaker cabinets, painted in this specific shade of navy blue that took us three tries to get right. You can't just shave off an inch and a half without ruining the finish. So he's standing there scratching his head, and I'm having to call the client and explain why their kitchen won't be finished for another two weeks while we wait for a new hood to be fabricated. And of course, they had a dinner party planned for the weekend to show off the new kitchen. I ended up having to buy them a gift card to a nice steakhouse just to smooth things over, which came right out of my overhead. 

So, yeah... days without stress? I don't think those really exist for me, so I don't know if the eating happens on those days or not.
Do you think the eating happens as a reaction to feeling overwhelmed or stressed from work?

I... I really couldn't say if it's a reaction to being overwhelmed. I just haven't paid that much attention to it, to be honest. It's just something that happens. 

Overwhelmed is kind of my baseline anyway, you know? Like, you want to talk about overwhelmed, you should see the permitting office downtown. It's a total joke. I was down there on Monday trying to pull a simple electrical permit for a panel upgrade. Just a standard 200-amp service, nothing crazy. And the lady at the desk—I think her name was Brenda, she always wears these awful oversized reading glasses on a chain—she tells me I have the wrong form. I've been using this same form for six years! Apparently, they updated the building code last month and didn't bother to tell any of the contractors. So I have to stand there in the lobby, filling out this new ten-page packet on a clipboard with a pen that barely works, while three other guys behind me in line are sighing and checking their watches. And then, when I finally hand it back, she tells me the inspector is out sick all week anyway. Just... unbelievable. 

So, I don't know. I guess I don't really know if the eating is because I'm stressed or overwhelmed. It's just hard to tell when everything is always such a mess.
Do you think eating is something you do to try and make yourself feel better when you're stressed?

I mean, maybe? I don't really think of it as trying to feel better. I don't know if it actually makes me feel anything, honestly. I haven't really stopped to analyze it like that. 

But talking about trying to feel better... you know what would make me feel better? If my suppliers would actually deliver what I ordered. I'm dealing with this lumber yard right now, and it's just a nightmare. We're framing a two-story addition, and I specifically ordered premium Doug Fir studs. I paid the upcharge and everything because the client is super picky about the walls being perfectly plumb and flat. So the truck shows up on site, they drop the load, and I go over to inspect it. Half the bunk is warped, bowed, or covered in bark edges. It looked like they just swept the floor of the mill and strapped it together. I called the rep, and he has the nerve to tell me that it's "within industry tolerance." Tolerance! I told him if I frame a wall with those studs, the drywall is going to look like a roller coaster. So now I've got my framing crew standing around on the clock, drinking coffee, while I have to drive my own truck down to the yard and hand-pick two hundred studs myself just to get the job moving. 

So yeah, I don't really know if the eating is about making myself feel better. I just haven't really noticed if that's why I do it.
Do you usually eat this way soon after a stressful event happens at work?

I'm not really sure about the timing, honestly. I don't know if it's right after something happens or later on. I just don't track it like that. 

Speaking of timing, though, you wouldn't believe the scheduling nightmare I'm dealing with right now on this bathroom remodel. Getting the trades lined up is like herding cats. I had the plumber scheduled for rough-in on Tuesday, right? He calls me Monday night at 8 PM to say his van broke down. So I have to push him to Wednesday. But the drywall guys were supposed to start Wednesday morning. So I have to call them and push them to Thursday. But Thursday is when the tile guy is supposed to prep the shower pan, and he's booked solid for the next three weeks after this job. If he doesn't get in there on Thursday, the whole project stalls for almost a month. So I'm on the phone for two hours trying to shuffle everyone around, begging favors, just to keep the timeline from completely falling apart. And then the client texts me asking if we're still on track to finish by the 15th. It's just constant putting out fires. 

But yeah, as for eating right after something stressful... I couldn't tell you. I just haven't paid attention to when it happens compared to work stuff.
Do you usually eat this way immediately after feeling stressed or overwhelmed at work?

I feel like you just asked me about the timing, and I... I really still don't know. I don't know if it's immediately after, or an hour after, or what. I just don't track the exact minutes after I get stressed to see when I eat. 

Honestly, the only thing I'm timing down to the minute these days is the concrete trucks. We had a foundation pour scheduled for yesterday morning, and the dispatcher sent the first truck forty-five minutes late. Do you know what happens to a pour when the second truck is sitting in traffic while the first batch is already setting up in the forms? You get a cold joint, and it's a structural nightmare. I had my concrete finishers literally standing around leaning on their floats, watching the mud get stiff. I was screaming at the batch plant on my cell phone while trying to help the pump operator clear a rock clog in the hose. We ended up having to vibrate the hell out of the mix just to get it to consolidate properly, and even then, I'm probably going to have to pay an engineer out of my own pocket to come out and sign off on it before we can start framing. 

So, yeah... immediately after? I have no idea. I just don't have the brain space to log when I'm eating compared to when I'm yelling at a concrete dispatcher.
Do you usually eat this way as soon as you feel stressed or overwhelmed at work?

Look, Doc, I... I don't know how many different ways I can say this. I really don't. You keep asking about when exactly it happens, like if it's right when I get stressed, and I just... I don't have an answer for you. I don't pay attention to the exact timeline of it all. 

It's like... it's like when clients ask me for an exact completion date before we've even opened up the walls. Like this kitchen demo we started last week. The homeowner wants to know the exact day the cabinets are going in, but we pulled down the drywall and found knob-and-tube wiring that nobody knew was there. And not just a little bit, I'm talking the whole first floor is wired like it's 1925. So now I have to stop everything, get an electrician in there to pull permits, rewire the whole grid, and get it inspected before we can even think about hanging drywall, let alone installing cabinets. And she's still texting me every morning asking, "Are the cabinets coming on the 12th?" I can't give an exact answer when there are a million variables I can't control! 

So, asking me if I eat the second I feel overwhelmed... I just can't give you a straight answer. I don't know. I'm sorry, I just don't know.
Do you think the act of eating is directly triggered by feeling stressed or overwhelmed?

I mean... I don't know if it's a direct trigger. I really haven't thought about it like a cause-and-effect kind of thing. I just know I get stressed and I know I eat like that sometimes, but if one directly causes the other... I'm not sure. 

It's kind of like trying to figure out why the lumber prices are doing what they're doing right now. Have you seen the cost of OSB lately? It's absolute robbery. I was pricing out a framing package for a two-story addition, and the supplier quoted me almost double what it would have cost six months ago. And they can't even guarantee the delivery date! They blame it on the mills, the mills blame it on the transport, the transport blames it on fuel prices... nobody actually knows what the direct trigger is for the price spike, it's just this massive chain reaction of headaches. And the worst part is, I have to go back to the client and explain why their budget just blew up before we even broke ground. Try having that conversation with a guy who just refinanced his house to pay for this. 

But yeah, as for the eating being triggered by the stress... I couldn't say for sure. I just haven't put the two together like that.
Do you think eating helps you cope with stress?

I don't know... does it help me cope? I honestly haven't really thought about whether it actually helps or not. I just do it. Coping is... well, I don't even know what coping looks like on my sites lately. 

Actually, speaking of coping, you should see my drywall crew trying to cope with the humidity this week. We’re trying to mud and tape this massive custom build out in the county, and the HVAC isn't hooked up yet because the mechanical subcontractor just decided to take a spontaneous fishing trip down to the Keys. So it’s like 90 degrees inside the house, 95 percent humidity, and the joint compound is just sitting wet on the walls for days. You can't sand wet mud! It just gums up the sanding screens and completely tears up the drywall paper. And the homeowner is breathing down my neck about the painting schedule, but how am I supposed to get the painters in when the walls feel like a damp sponge? It's a total disaster, and I'm the one who has to eat the delay costs. 

So... yeah, I don't know if the eating helps me cope with any of that. I really couldn't tell you. I'm not sure it does anything at all, honestly.
Do you think the eating happens as a direct result of feeling stressed or overwhelmed?

Doc, I feel like we are just going in circles here. I really do not know if it is a direct result. I just do not have a clear answer for you on that. 

It is honestly like trying to figure out who messed up the plumbing rough-in on this master bath I am managing right now. My plumber called me yesterday saying the floor joists are running the exact wrong way for the main drainage line. And you try to find the direct cause of that, right? But the architect blames the structural engineer, the engineer blames the drafter, and nobody wants to take the hit. There is no one direct reason it happened, it is just a massive headache. So now I have to figure out if we are going to frame out a drop ceiling in the living room underneath just to hide the pipes, which is a total nightmare because the client specifically requested exposed beams. Do you have any idea how hard it is to source authentic reclaimed barn wood beams right now? I have a guy upstate who usually drives them down to my sites, but his flatbed blew a transmission last week and he is stuck waiting on parts, so now I am scrambling to find a local mill that will not overcharge me. 

So... yeah. I am just putting out fires all day. I do not know if the eating is a direct result of the stress. I really just do not know.
Is the eating something that happens only when you are feeling stressed or overwhelmed?

I mean, no, not only when I'm stressed. I don't think so, anyway. It happens other times too, I guess. It's not like I have a schedule for it or only do it when things go wrong. 

Speaking of things going wrong, though, you wouldn't believe the absolute circus I walked into this morning. We're pouring the foundation for this triplex, right? And I told the concrete dispatch—very clearly, I might add—that we needed the first truck there by 6:00 AM sharp because the heat index is supposed to hit triple digits by noon, and you do not want concrete curing too fast in that kind of heat. It cracks, it shrinks, it's a structural nightmare. So I get there at 5:45, coffee in hand, ready to go. My guys are there, rebar is tied, forms are braced. 6:00 comes, no truck. 6:30, no truck. I call dispatch, and the guy has the nerve to tell me my order was bumped because some commercial crew down by the highway needed an emergency pour for a retaining wall. An emergency pour! What does that even mean? Did the wall suddenly decide to collapse overnight? 

So I'm standing there, the sun is coming up, my crew is just leaning on their shovels on the clock, and I'm losing money by the minute. I finally got a truck out there by 9:00, but by then it's already 85 degrees and we're spraying the forms down with a hose just trying to keep the temperature down. I swear, if this foundation cracks, I'm sending the bill straight to that dispatcher. 

But, uh, what were we talking about? Oh, right. The eating. Yeah, no, it's not just when I'm stressed. It just kind of happens whenever.
